text:
mia chen: FYI CI is red on master because the audit-event validation step is failing after the RBAC/audit schema change in #4112. failing tests look like a golden-fixture mismatch.

mia chen: paste of the CI snippet:
```
FAIL tests/validation/test_golden_fixtures.py::test_all_fixtures
E   AssertionError: fixture 'customer_create_with_kms.json' differs from schema
E   - missing required property 'kms_key_id'
E   - unexpected property 'actor_role_v1'
```

mia chen: I didn't touch fixtures in the PR, only the schema (added kms_key_id, renamed actor_role -> actor_role_v2). tagging @arjun @sophia for context.

arjun patel: looking. this smells like schema drift + old golden fixtures. two possibilities: schema tightened and we need to migrate golden fixtures, or validator became stricter. can you paste the schema diff? also which CI job is failing (unit vs integration)?

mia chen: failing job is `audit-validators` (unit). schema diff is tiny, added `kms_key_id` (string, optional) but also changed `actor_role` enum values and made the property name explicit. gist of schema change:
```
- "actor_role": {"type":"string"}
+ "actor_role_v2": {"type":"string","enum":["user","service","system"]}
+ "kms_key_id": {"type":"string"}
```

sophia king: heads up: some customers send legacy payloads with actor_role (without _v2). the validator used to coerce unknown fields; the new schema removes that and now the validator flags unexpected properties. that explains `unexpected property 'actor_role_v1'` in the log.

ben liu: agreed. two action items: 1) update golden fixtures to canonical v2 format (and add migration script), 2) make CI clearer: validator should run in two modes in CI — strict for internal-only events, and permissive for customer-facing events where we also log a normalization warning. otherwise we'll keep flapping.

olivia park: devops-bot already fired an alert to #eng-ci: `audit-validators` failed 3 times in the last hour. I'm going to pin this for pager duty if it keeps failing. :warning:

audit-bot: System: Audit schema deployed: audit_event_v2.json at 2026-03-20T09:12Z. All validators need to load new schema version or opt-in to compatibility layer.

arjun patel: we need a short-term fix to unbreak master: either revert schema change in the PR or update the CI job to accept legacy fields for 48h while we migrate fixtures. preference: patch CI so it accepts both names using a compatibility transform step that canonicalizes payloads before validation.

mia chen: i can push a compatibility transform. plan: add a pre-validation hook scripts/audit/compat_transform.py that renames actor_role -> actor_role_v2 and fills kms_key_id from event.metadata.kms if present. will also run local golden update command.

ben liu: please also add a test for the transform. sample command to reproduce locally:
```
# run validator with compatibility hook
python -m scripts.audit.validate --fixtures fixtures/golden/*.json --schema schemas/audit_event_v2.json --compat scripts/audit/compat_transform.py
```

sophia king: long-term: we should add a CI gate that compares raw incoming production audit events (sanitized) against golden fixtures nightly and surfaces regressions to a dedicated Slack channel before they hit a PR. that would catch schema drift earlier.

olivia park: I'll open a ticket with infra to add the nightly job and a lightweight dashboard. also will add a temporary CI label on the failing job so PRs don't get blocked by this compatibility window.

mia chen: implemented compat_transform locally, tests pass. opening a tiny PR to change the CI job to include the transform step. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4220

devops-bot: CI update: audit-validators (with compat hook) queued by mia chen for branch `fix/compat-transform`. build 1283.

mia chen: if everyone is OK with the compatibility hook I'll merge and then follow up by migrating golden fixtures and removing permissive mode in 48h.

arjun patel: sounds good. after merge, run the golden-update script and add a one-liner in the PR description documenting the fixture migration. also tag customer-privacy to confirm no sensitive KMS values are landing in fixtures.

sophia king: noted. I'll also add an evaluator check that flags when enum values change upstream and requires explicit approval from eng-security before schema rollout.

mia chen: thanks all, will merge the hook now and follow up with migration PRs. :thumbsup!
